title: Atlassian Automates Root Cause Analysis by Correlating Metrics, Logs and Traces
gist: Atlassian, publishing through the CNCF, reframes root cause analysis as a multi-signal correlation problem across signal type, time and topology, using OpenTelemetry-derived service maps built from real production traffic to narrow the search space and produce ranked, evidence-backed hypotheses. The binding constraint in cloud-native reliability has shifted from collecting telemetry to correlating it fast enough, and Grafana Cloud and Dynatrace are chasing the same prize with knowledge-graph and event-correlation approaches.

themes.theme: Correlation, not collection, is the bottleneck

insights.claim: As cloud-native systems become more distributed, the challenge is no longer collecting telemetry but correlating it quickly enough to support effective incident response.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Value in observability is migrating from ingest-and-store (volume-priced) to correlation and reasoning — a margin and pricing-model shift for the whole category.
insights.locator: As cloud-native systems become more distributed

insights.claim: A 2026 CNCF community survey found many organisations still run multiple observability platforms simultaneously, forcing engineers to bridge metrics, logs and traces across different tools manually.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Persistent multi-vendor fragmentation is the demand driver for correlation layers — and a consolidation thesis for whoever can sit above all of them.
insights.locator: That problem is amplified by tool fragmentation.

insights.claim: The manual process of switching between dashboards and tools to connect individual telemetry signals into a coherent explanation is one of the most time-consuming parts of incident response.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Quantifiable engineer-hours during outages are the ROI case automated RCA vendors will sell against — MTTR is the metric to watch.
insights.locator: the work addresses one of the most time-consuming parts

insights.claim: The ability to automatically transform thousands of disconnected signals into a small number of evidence-backed hypotheses may become one of the most valuable capabilities in modern reliability engineering.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Frames automated RCA as the next high-value observability feature — a differentiator to test incumbents' roadmaps against.
insights.locator: As cloud-native architectures continue to add services

themes.theme: Narrowing the search space with real traffic graphs

insights.claim: Rather than analysing every service in a large production environment, Atlassian's system uses OpenTelemetry-derived service maps to isolate only the subset of services involved in the affected user journey.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Search-space reduction is what makes RCA computationally tractable at scale — the step that determines whether these systems work beyond demo environments.
insights.locator: Atlassian's approach begins by reducing the search space.

insights.claim: The dependency graph is built from actual production traffic using parent-child relationships between spans, showing how services communicate in practice rather than relying on static architectural documentation.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Architecture diagrams are treated as unreliable ground truth; trace-derived topology is the asset, which entrenches OpenTelemetry instrumentation as a prerequisite.
insights.locator: The dependency graph is built from actual production traffic

insights.claim: Atlassian treats root cause analysis fundamentally as a multi-signal correlation problem across three axes simultaneously: signal type, time, and topology.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A clean mental model for evaluating any automated-RCA claim — a vendor covering only one or two axes is doing anomaly detection, not RCA.
insights.locator: The system treats root cause analysis fundamentally

insights.claim: Different detection methods are applied per signal type — metrics checked for changes in rates, errors and duration; traces analysed for exceptions, latency and structural changes; logs grouped to surface new or unusual error patterns — then all findings are converted into a common anomaly format.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A shared anomaly schema is the integration point that lets a correlation layer sit above heterogeneous tools — the architectural key to displacing point solutions.
insights.locator: The system applies different detection methods

insights.claim: Anomalies occurring close together in time are grouped into a potential failure sequence — for example a database issue followed by application timeouts and frontend errors treated as one incident — with sequence fingerprinting used to collapse duplicates of recurring failure patterns.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Fingerprinting recurring patterns is what turns alert volume into a manageable stream; directly attacks alert fatigue, the top complaint driving observability churn.
insights.locator: Anomalies occurring close together in time

insights.claim: Temporal proximity alone cannot establish causation, so the system additionally uses service dependencies and the order in which anomalies appeared, tracing upstream from affected services to identify possible fault origins.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Distinguishes real causal inference from correlation-dashboard marketing — the test to apply to competing AIOps claims.
insights.locator: Time alone cannot establish causation, however.

insights.claim: The output summarises suspected cause, affected services and supporting telemetry rather than presenting a raw anomaly list, so engineers review evidence and validate the diagnosis before acting.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop with explicit evidence is the design pattern that gets automation past SRE trust barriers — a gating requirement for adoption.
insights.locator: The output summarises the suspected cause

themes.theme: Competitive field: Grafana, Dynatrace and modularity

insights.claim: Grafana Cloud is building a knowledge-graph approach correlating telemetry with infrastructure relationships to surface likely causes, while Dynatrace correlates events from multiple sources alongside logs, metrics and traces to identify problems and likely impact.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Automated RCA is now a contested feature across commercial observability vendors, not a differentiator — expect it to be table stakes and priced in within a cycle.
insights.locator: Commercial observability platforms are pursuing similar goals.

insights.claim: Atlassian's distinguishing choice is a modular, signal-normalised pipeline in which individual anomaly detectors evolve independently while a single correlation layer reasons over the resulting evidence.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Decoupling detectors from the correlation layer is the architecture that survives detector churn — a durability advantage over monolithic vendor engines.
insights.locator: The difference in Atlassian's model is its detailed focus

insights.claim: Atlassian published this incident-response architecture through the Cloud Native Computing Foundation rather than as a proprietary product announcement.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Open publication commoditises the technique and pressures vendors whose RCA is sold as proprietary secret sauce.
insights.locator: Published through the Cloud Native Computing Foundation

themes.theme: LLM-orchestrated iterative investigation as the next step

insights.claim: Atlassian is exploring LLM-based orchestration to make RCA iterative, with an agent requesting additional telemetry, testing competing hypotheses and adapting its investigation to available evidence instead of producing one fixed answer.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Agentic investigation would make telemetry query volume itself a variable cost — a new consumption driver for observability backends.
insights.locator: Atlassian says they are now exploring the next step

insights.claim: Agentic RCA systems will require explicit controls around rate limits, execution environments and evidence provenance before they can run against production telemetry.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Provenance and sandboxing are the gating engineering work — the reason agentic observability will lag the marketing by quarters.
insights.locator: Atlassian notes, however, that such systems will require controls

insights.claim: The central risk in automated root cause analysis is that systems remain explainable enough for engineers to trust and grounded enough in real telemetry that automation accelerates understanding rather than generating a more convincing guess.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Plausible-but-wrong RCA is worse than none during an outage; trust, not accuracy benchmarks, is the adoption bottleneck for AIOps vendors.
insights.locator: The challenge will be ensuring that those systems remain explainable
